name: Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
description: Matter, SI units, significant figures, laws of combination, mole concept, empirical formula, stoichiometry and concentration terms

cards.term: Define chemistry.
cards.definition: The branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structure and reactions of material substances

cards.text: Chemistry arose from the search for the {{c1::philosopher’s stone (Paras)}}, to turn base metals into gold, and the {{c2::elixir of life}}, to grant immortality.

cards.term: In what forms did chemistry develop during 1300–1600 CE?
cards.definition: Alchemy and Iatrochemistry

cards.term: Ancient Indian names for chemistry?
cards.definition: Rasayan Shastra, Rastantra, Ras Kriya or Rasvidya

cards.term: What did the Harappans use to harden copper?
cards.definition: Tin and arsenic

cards.term: What was faience?
cards.definition: A sort of glass made by the Harappans, used in ornaments

cards.term: Which ancient text mentions preparing sulphuric acid, nitric acid and metal oxides?
cards.definition: Charaka Samhita

cards.term: Which text describes the preparation of gunpowder?
cards.definition: Rasopanishada

cards.term: Nagarjuna’s work on mercury compounds?
cards.definition: Rasratnakar

cards.term: Who discovered mercury sulphide and is credited with inventing soap?
cards.definition: Chakrapani (used mustard oil and alkalies)

cards.term: Who first proposed an atomic theory in India, and what did he call atoms?
cards.definition: Acharya Kanda (Kashyap, ~600 BCE), in the Vaiseshika Sutras; atoms = "Paramãnu"

cards.term: Properties of Kanda’s Paramãnu?
cards.definition: Eternal, indestructible, spherical, suprasensible and in motion; could form pairs or triplets

cards.term: Bhasmas of Charaka Samhita are now known to contain?
cards.definition: Metal nanoparticles (extreme particle-size reduction = nanotechnology)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT says paper was known in India "in the 17th century" per I-tsing. Actually?
cards.definition: I-tsing travelled in the 7th century CE; "17th" is a typo

cards.term: Two anticancer drugs named in NCERT?
cards.definition: Cisplatin and taxol

cards.term: Drug used for AIDS patients?
cards.definition: AZT (azidothymidine)

cards.term: Examples of new materials designed with chemistry?
cards.definition: Superconducting ceramics, conducting polymers, optical fibres

cards.term: Refrigerants replaced because of ozone depletion?
cards.definition: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons)

cards.term: Define matter.
cards.definition: Anything that has mass and occupies space

cards.term: States of matter: shape and volume
cards.definition: Solid: Definite volume and definite shape; Liquid: Definite volume, no definite shape; Gas: Neither definite volume nor shape

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
States of matter

Definite shape / volume?

Solid?
Liquid?
Gas?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
States of matter

Definite shape / volume?

SolidDefinite volume and definite shape
LiquidDefinite volume, no definite shape
GasNeither definite volume nor shape

cards.term: Particle arrangement in the three states?
cards.definition: Solid: close, orderly, little movement. Liquid: close but mobile. Gas: far apart, fast.

cards.term: How are the states interconverted?
cards.definition: By changing temperature and pressure

cards.term: Figure 1.2 · Classification of matter
Pure substance vs mixture?
cards.definition: Pure substance: all particles of the same chemical nature, fixed composition. Mixture: two or more substances in any ratio (variable composition).

cards.term: Homogeneous vs heterogeneous mixture?
cards.definition: Homogeneous: uniform composition throughout (sugar solution, air). Heterogeneous: not uniform (salt + sugar, grains with dirt).

cards.term: How are components of a mixture separated?
cards.definition: By physical methods: hand-picking, filtration, crystallisation, distillation

cards.term: Is air a compound or a mixture? (trap)
cards.definition: A homogeneous mixture: its composition varies and components keep their properties

cards.term: Element vs compound?
cards.definition: Element: only one type of atom (as atoms or molecules). Compound: atoms of different elements in a fixed ratio; separable only by chemical methods.

cards.term: Elements whose particles are atoms vs molecules?
cards.definition: Atoms: Na, Cu. Diatomic molecules: H₂, N₂, O₂.

cards.term: Identify the molecules shown.
cards.definition: Water (H₂O: 2 H + 1 O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂: 1 C + 2 O)

cards.term: How does water show that compound properties differ from its elements?
cards.definition: H₂ burns with a pop and O₂ supports combustion, but water extinguishes fire

cards.term: Physical vs chemical property?
cards.definition: Physical: measured without changing identity (colour, m.p., density). Chemical: needs a chemical change (combustibility, acidity).

cards.term: When and by whom was the SI established?
cards.definition: In 1960 by the 11th CGPM (General Conference on Weights and Measures)

cards.term: Treaty that created the CGPM?
cards.definition: The Metre Convention, Paris, 1875

cards.term: Which Indian lab maintains the national standards of measurement?
cards.definition: National Physical Laboratory (NPL), New Delhi

cards.term: The seven SI base units
cards.definition: Length: metre (m); Mass: kilogram (kg); Time: second (s); Electric current: ampere (A); Thermodynamic temperature: kelvin (K); Amount of substance: mole (mol); Luminous intensity: candela (cd)

cards.term: Mnemonic for the 7 SI base quantities?
cards.definition: "LMT CTAL": Length, Mass, Time, Current, Temperature, Amount, Luminous intensity

cards.term: How is the kilogram defined now (Table 1.2)?
cards.definition: By fixing the Planck constant h = 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J s

cards.term: Which constant fixes the kelvin? The ampere?
cards.definition: Kelvin: Boltzmann constant k = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹. Ampere: elementary charge e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

cards.term: What defines the second?
cards.definition: The caesium-133 hyperfine frequency fixed at 9192631770 Hz

cards.term: Update: NCERT’s box says the kilogram standard is still a Pt-Ir cylinder. Current status?
cards.definition: Since 20 May 2019 the kg is defined through the Planck constant; the Pt-Ir prototype is retired (Table 1.2 already uses the new definition)

cards.term: Why was Pt-Ir chosen for the old kilogram prototype?
cards.definition: Highly resistant to chemical attack, so its mass stays constant

cards.term: 1983 definition of the metre?
cards.definition: Path travelled by light in vacuum in 1/299 792 458 of a second

cards.text: SI prefixes: pico = {{c1::10⁻¹²}}, nano = {{c2::10⁻⁹}}, micro = {{c3::10⁻⁶}}, milli = 10⁻³.
SI prefixes: kilo = 10³, mega = {{c1::10⁶}}, giga = {{c2::10⁹}}, tera = {{c3::10¹²}}.

cards.term: Full list of SI prefixes (Table 1.3)?
cards.definition: yocto 10⁻²⁴ … yotta 10²⁴

cards.term: Mass vs weight?
cards.definition: Mass: amount of matter, constant. Weight: force of gravity on it, varies with place.

cards.term: Instrument for accurate mass in the lab?
cards.definition: Analytical balance

cards.extra: The litre is not an SI unit; SI volume is m³.

cards.term: How many litres in 1 m³?
cards.definition: 1000 L (1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³)

cards.term: Name the volume measuring devices.
cards.definition: Burette, pipette, graduated cylinder, volumetric flask (to prepare a known volume of solution)

cards.term: SI unit of density, and the unit chemists use?
cards.definition: kg m⁻³; chemists use g cm⁻³

cards.term: What does a higher density tell you?
cards.definition: Particles are more closely packed

cards.term: Relation between °F and °C?
Relation between K and °C?

cards.text: Water freezes at {{c1::273.15 K}} = 0 °C = {{c2::32 °F}} and boils at 373 K = 100 °C = {{c3::212 °F}}.

cards.term: At what temperature are °C and °F equal? (trap)
cards.definition: −40°: solve \( x = \frac{9}{5}x + 32 \)

cards.term: Can temperature be negative on the Kelvin scale?
cards.definition: No; negative values are possible only on the Celsius (and Fahrenheit) scale

cards.term: Human body temperature on the three scales?
cards.definition: 37 °C = 310 K = 98.6 °F

cards.term: Form of scientific notation?
cards.definition: \( N \times 10^{n} \), where N (digit term) is from 1.000… to 9.999…

cards.term: Write 232.508 and 0.00016 in scientific notation.
Rule for adding numbers in scientific notation?
cards.definition: First bring them to the same exponent, then add the digit terms

cards.term: What are significant figures?
cards.definition: Meaningful digits known with certainty plus one uncertain (estimated) digit

cards.text: Sig-fig rules: all {{c1::non-zero}} digits count; zeros {{c2::before}} the first non-zero digit do not; zeros {{c3::between}} non-zero digits do.

cards.term: Are trailing zeros significant?
cards.definition: Only if there is a decimal point: 0.200 has 3; 100 has 1; 100.0 has 4

cards.term: How many sig figs in an exact count like "20 eggs"?
cards.definition: Infinite (exact numbers)

cards.term: Sig figs in 4.01 × 10² and 8.256 × 10⁻³?
cards.definition: 3 and 4 (all digits in scientific notation are significant)
2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 5

cards.term: How do you write 100 with exactly 2 sig figs?
Precision vs accuracy?
cards.definition: Precision: closeness of repeated measurements to each other. Accuracy: closeness to the true value.

cards.term: Precision vs accuracy data
cards.definition: A: 1.95, 1.93: Precise, not accurate; B: 1.94, 2.05: Neither; C: 2.01, 1.99: Precise and accurate

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Table 1.4 · true value 2.00 g

B: 1.94, 2.05?
C: 2.01, 1.99?

Table 1.4 · true value 2.00 g

Precise? Accurate?

A: 1.95, 1.93Precise, not accurate
B: 1.94, 2.05Neither
C: 2.01, 1.99Precise and accurate

cards.term: Rule for sig figs in addition/subtraction?
cards.definition: Result has no more decimal places than the number with the fewest (12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 = 31.1)

cards.term: Rule for sig figs in multiplication/division?
cards.definition: Result has no more significant figures than the least precise number (2.5 × 1.25 = 3.1)

cards.text: Rounding when the dropped digit is exactly 5: if the preceding digit is {{c1::even}}, leave it; if {{c2::odd}}, add one. So 6.35 → {{c3::6.4}}, 6.25 → {{c4::6.2}}.

cards.term: Other names of dimensional analysis?
cards.definition: Factor label method or unit factor method

cards.term: What is a unit factor?
cards.definition: A ratio equal to 1, e.g. 2.54 cm / 1 in; multiply so unwanted units cancel

cards.term: Convert 2 L to m³

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Dimensional analysis

A jug holds 2 L of milk. Volume in m³?

1 L = 1000 cm³; 1 m = 100 cm.
  1. 2 L = 2 × 1000 cm³ = 2000 cm³
  2. ?
  3. 2000 cm³ × 1 m³/10⁶ cm³ = 2 × 10⁻³ m³
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Dimensional analysis

A jug holds 2 L of milk. Volume in m³?

1 L = 1000 cm³; 1 m = 100 cm.
  1. 2 L = 2 × 1000 cm³ = 2000 cm³
  2. (1 m / 100 cm)³ = 1 m³ / 10⁶ cm³
  3. 2000 cm³ × 1 m³/10⁶ cm³ = 2 × 10⁻³ m³

cards.term: Seconds in 2 days?
cards.definition: 2 × 24 × 60 × 60 = 172800 s

cards.term: Distance covered by light in 2.00 ns (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)? (Ex 1.22)
Law of conservation of mass: who and when?
cards.definition: Antoine Lavoisier, 1789: matter can neither be created nor destroyed

cards.term: Law of definite proportions: who, and statement?
cards.definition: Joseph Proust: a given compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by weight

cards.term: Compound Proust used to prove definite proportions?
cards.definition: Cupric carbonate, natural vs synthetic: Cu 51.35%, C 9.74%, O 38.91% in both

cards.term: Another name for the law of definite proportions?
cards.definition: Law of definite composition

cards.term: Law of multiple proportions: who, when, statement?
cards.definition: Dalton, 1803: when two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a small whole-number ratio

cards.term: NCERT example of multiple proportions?
cards.definition: H₂O and H₂O₂: 16 g and 32 g O per 2 g H → 1 : 2
Multiple proportions: O per 14 g N = 16, 32, 16, 40 → 2 : 4 : 2 : 5

cards.term: Gay Lussac’s law (1808)?
cards.definition: Gases combine or are produced in a simple ratio by volume at the same T and P

cards.term: H₂ + O₂ → water vapour: volumes?
cards.definition: 100 mL + 50 mL → 100 mL (2 : 1 : 2)

cards.term: Gay Lussac’s law is really which law, by volume?
cards.definition: The law of definite proportions by volume

cards.term: Avogadro’s law (1811)?
cards.definition: Equal volumes of all gases at the same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules

cards.term: What key idea let Avogadro explain Gay Lussac’s data?
cards.definition: Distinguishing atoms from molecules: H₂ and O₂ are diatomic

cards.term: Why was Avogadro ignored at first?
cards.definition: Dalton and others believed atoms of the same kind could not combine, so O₂/H₂ molecules couldn’t exist

cards.term: Who revived Avogadro’s work, where and when?
cards.definition: Stanislao Cannizzaro, first international chemistry conference, Karlsruhe, 1860

cards.term: Dalton’s book (1808)?
cards.definition: "A New System of Chemical Philosophy"

cards.text: Dalton: matter consists of {{c1::indivisible atoms}}; atoms of an element have identical {{c2::mass}}; compounds form in a {{c3::fixed ratio}}; reactions only {{c4::reorganise}} atoms.

cards.term: What could Dalton’s theory NOT explain?
cards.definition: The law of gaseous volumes, and why atoms combine

cards.term: Greek philosopher behind "a-tomio" (indivisible)?
cards.definition: Democritus (460–370 BC)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT prints Dalton’s dates as 1776–1884. Actual?
cards.definition: 1766–1844 (NCERT itself says 1766–1844 on page 3)

cards.term: Update: which of Dalton’s postulates are known to be wrong today?
cards.definition: Atoms are divisible (e, p, n); atoms of an element can differ in mass (isotopes)

cards.term: Present standard for atomic masses, adopted when?
cards.definition: Carbon-12, assigned exactly 12 amu, in 1961

cards.term: Define 1 amu.
cards.definition: Exactly 1/12 of the mass of one ¹²C atom = 1.66056 × 10⁻²⁴ g

cards.term: What replaced "amu"?
cards.definition: u (unified mass)

cards.term: Mass of an H atom in u?
Why is the atomic mass in the periodic table not a whole number?
cards.definition: It is the average atomic mass, weighted by the natural abundance of isotopes

cards.term: Average atomic mass of Cl

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Average atomic mass

Average atomic mass of chlorine? (Ex 1.9)

³⁵Cl: 75.77%, 34.9689 u. ³⁷Cl: 24.23%, 36.9659 u.
  1. 0.7577 × 34.9689 = 26.496
  2. 0.2423 × 36.9659 = 8.957
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Average atomic mass

Average atomic mass of chlorine? (Ex 1.9)

³⁵Cl: 75.77%, 34.9689 u. ³⁷Cl: 24.23%, 36.9659 u.
  1. 0.7577 × 34.9689 = 26.496
  2. 0.2423 × 36.9659 = 8.957
  3. Sum = 35.45 u

cards.term: Average atomic mass of carbon from its isotopes?
cards.definition: 12.011 u (¹²C 98.892%, ¹³C 1.108%, ¹⁴C trace)

cards.term: Why does NCERT’s carbon table show ¹⁴C as 2 × 10⁻¹⁰ but use 2 × 10⁻¹² in the sum?
cards.definition: The table is in per cent; the sum uses a fraction (÷ 100). Same quantity; ¹⁴C adds nothing measurable.

cards.term: Define molecular mass.
cards.definition: Sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule

cards.term: Molecular mass of CH₄ and H₂O?
cards.definition: CH₄ = 16.043 u; H₂O = 18.02 u

cards.term: Molecular mass of glucose C₆H₁₂O₆? (Problem 1.1)
Why "formula mass" for NaCl, not molecular mass?
cards.definition: NaCl has no discrete molecules: it is a 3D network of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions

cards.term: Coordination in NaCl crystal?
cards.definition: Each Na⁺ is surrounded by six Cl⁻ and vice versa

cards.term: Formula mass of NaCl?
cards.definition: 23.0 + 35.5 = 58.5 u

cards.term: Define one mole (current SI).
cards.definition: Exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons…)

cards.term: What is the Avogadro constant?
cards.definition: \( N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23} \) mol⁻¹, the number of entities in one mole

cards.term: How was the number of atoms in 12 g of ¹²C found?
cards.definition: 12 g ÷ mass of one ¹²C atom (1.992648 × 10⁻²³ g, by mass spectrometer) = 6.022 × 10²³

cards.term: Everyday analogy for the mole? (intuition)
cards.definition: Like a dozen (12) or a gross (144): a counting unit, just a very large one

cards.term: Define molar mass.
cards.definition: Mass of one mole of a substance in grams; numerically equal to atomic/molecular/formula mass in u

cards.term: Key mole relations (exam formula sheet)?
cards.definition: \( n = \frac{m}{M} = \frac{N}{N_A} = \frac{V}{22.7} \) (V of gas in L at STP)

cards.term: Moles of C atoms, H atoms and molecules in 3 mol C₂H₆? (Ex 1.10)
cards.definition: 6 mol C, 18 mol H, 1.807 × 10²⁴ molecules

cards.term: Number of atoms in 52 mol Ar, 52 u He, 52 g He? (classic)
cards.definition: \( 52 N_A \); 13 atoms (52/4); \( 13 N_A \)

cards.term: Trap: "1 mole of O" vs "1 mole of O₂"?
cards.definition: 1 mol O atoms = 16 g; 1 mol O₂ molecules = 32 g. Always name the entity.

cards.term: Formula for mass % of an element?
cards.definition: Mass % = (mass of element in 1 mol of compound ÷ molar mass) × 100

cards.term: Mass % of H and O in water?
cards.definition: H = 2.016/18.02 = 11.18%; O = 88.79%

cards.term: Mass % of C, H, O in ethanol (C₂H₅OH)?
cards.definition: C 52.14%, H 13.13%, O 34.73%

cards.term: Use of percentage composition for a known compound?
cards.definition: To check the purity of a sample

cards.term: Empirical vs molecular formula?
cards.definition: Empirical: simplest whole-number ratio of atoms. Molecular: exact number of each atom.

cards.text: Empirical formula steps: mass % → grams (take {{c1::100 g}}) → {{c2::moles}} (÷ atomic mass) → divide by the {{c3::smallest}} → whole numbers.

cards.term: How do you get the molecular formula from the empirical one?
cards.definition: n = molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass; multiply the empirical formula by n

cards.term: Empirical to molecular formula
cards.definition: CH₂Cl → C₂H₄Cl₂

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 1.2

H 4.07%, C 24.27%, Cl 71.65%; M = 98.96 g. Formulas?

Take 100 g.
  1. mol H = 4.04, C = 2.021, Cl = 2.021
  2. Ratio H:C:Cl = 2:1:1 → CH₂Cl
  3. EF mass 49.48; n = 98.96/49.48 = 2
  4. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 1.2

H 4.07%, C 24.27%, Cl 71.65%; M = 98.96 g. Formulas?

Take 100 g.
  1. mol H = 4.04, C = 2.021, Cl = 2.021
  2. Ratio H:C:Cl = 2:1:1 → CH₂Cl
  3. EF mass 49.48; n = 98.96/49.48 = 2
  4. Molecular formula C₂H₄Cl₂

cards.term: Empirical formula of iron oxide with 69.9% Fe, 30.1% O? (Ex 1.3)
cards.definition: Fe 1.25 : O 1.88 = 1 : 1.5 = 2 : 3 → Fe₂O₃

cards.term: Trap: mole ratio comes out 1 : 1.5 or 1 : 1.33. What next?
cards.definition: Multiply all by 2 or 3 to reach whole numbers; don’t round 1.5 to 2

cards.term: Meaning of "stoichiometry"?
cards.definition: Greek stoicheion (element) + metron (measure): calculating masses/volumes of reactants and products

cards.term: What are stoichiometric coefficients?
cards.definition: The numbers before formulas in a balanced equation: they give molecule and mole ratios

cards.term: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O: read it in mass and in volume.
cards.definition: 16 g CH₄ + 64 g O₂ → 44 g CO₂ + 36 g H₂O; 22.7 L + 45.4 L → 22.7 L + 45.4 L

cards.term: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP in NCERT?
cards.definition: 22.7 L (STP = 273.15 K, 1 bar)

cards.term: Update: 22.4 L or 22.7 L?
cards.definition: 22.4 L is at 0 °C and 1 atm (old STP); 22.7 L at 1 bar (IUPAC). Check which STP the question uses.

cards.term: Rule you must never break while balancing?
cards.definition: Never change subscripts in formulas; only change coefficients

cards.term: Balance P₄ + O₂ → P₄O₁₀.
cards.definition: P₄ + 5O₂ → P₄O₁₀

cards.term: Balance the combustion of propane.
cards.definition: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O

cards.term: Water from combustion of 16 g CH₄? (Problem 1.3)
cards.definition: 1 mol CH₄ → 2 mol H₂O = 36 g

cards.term: Moles of CH₄ needed for 22 g CO₂? (Problem 1.4)
cards.definition: 22/44 = 0.5 mol CO₂ ← 0.5 mol CH₄

cards.term: Define limiting reagent.
cards.definition: The reactant consumed first; it limits the amount of product formed

cards.term: Limiting reagent in NH₃ synthesis
cards.definition: H₂ limiting; 56.1 kg NH₃

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 1.5

50.0 kg N₂ + 10.0 kg H₂ → NH₃. Limiting reagent and NH₃?

N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃
  1. mol N₂ = 50000/28 = 1786; mol H₂ = 10000/2.016 = 4960
  2. ?
  3. NH₃ = 4960 × 2/3 = 3307 mol
  4. × 17 g = 56.1 kg NH₃
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 1.5

50.0 kg N₂ + 10.0 kg H₂ → NH₃. Limiting reagent and NH₃?

N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃
  1. mol N₂ = 50000/28 = 1786; mol H₂ = 10000/2.016 = 4960
  2. H₂ needed = 3 × 1786 = 5360 > 4960, so H₂ is limiting
  3. NH₃ = 4960 × 2/3 = 3307 mol
  4. × 17 g = 56.1 kg NH₃

cards.term: Quick test for limiting reagent? (trick)
cards.definition: Divide each reactant’s moles by its coefficient; the smallest quotient is limiting

cards.term: A + B₂ → AB₂: 2 mol A + 3 mol B₂. Limiting? (Ex 1.23)
cards.definition: A is limiting (needs only 2 mol B₂; 1 mol B₂ left over)

cards.term: CO₂ from 2 mol C burnt in 16 g O₂? (Ex 1.4 iii)
cards.definition: 16 g O₂ = 0.5 mol, so O₂ limits: 0.5 mol = 22 g CO₂

cards.term: Copper obtainable from 100 g CuSO₄? (Ex 1.7)

cards.text: Four ways to express concentration in NCERT: {{c1::mass per cent}}, {{c2::mole fraction}}, {{c3::molarity}} and {{c4::molality}}.

cards.term: Mass per cent of solute?
cards.definition: (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100

cards.term: 2 g of A in 18 g water: mass %? (Problem 1.6)
cards.definition: 2/20 × 100 = 10%

cards.term: Mole fraction of A in a mixture of A and B?
cards.definition: \( x_A = \frac{n_A}{n_A + n_B} \); the sum of all mole fractions = 1

cards.term: Define molarity (M).
cards.definition: Moles of solute per litre of solution

cards.term: Define molality (m).
cards.definition: Moles of solute per kg of solvent

cards.term: Which of molarity or molality changes with temperature, and why?
cards.definition: Molarity changes (volume expands); molality does not (mass is unaffected)

cards.term: Molarity of 4 g NaOH in 250 mL solution? (Problem 1.7)
cards.definition: 0.1 mol / 0.250 L = 0.4 M

cards.term: Dilution formula?
cards.definition: \( M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2 \) (moles of solute unchanged)

cards.term: Volume of 1 M NaOH needed to make 1 L of 0.2 M?
cards.definition: 200 mL, diluted to 1 L

cards.term: What is a stock solution?
cards.definition: A solution of known higher concentration that is diluted to the desired one

cards.term: Molarity to molality

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 1.8

3 M NaCl, density 1.25 g/mL. Molality?

Take 1 L of solution.
  1. Mass NaCl = 3 × 58.5 = 175.5 g
  2. Mass solution = 1000 × 1.25 = 1250 g
  3. ?
  4. m = 3 / 1.0745 = 2.79 m
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 1.8

3 M NaCl, density 1.25 g/mL. Molality?

Take 1 L of solution.
  1. Mass NaCl = 3 × 58.5 = 175.5 g
  2. Mass solution = 1000 × 1.25 = 1250 g
  3. Mass water = 1250 − 175.5 = 1074.5 g
  4. m = 3 / 1.0745 = 2.79 m

cards.term: Correction: Problem 1.8 in NCERT prints "1250 − 75.5". Right?
cards.definition: 1250 − 175.5 = 1074.5 g (the answer 2.79 m uses this)

cards.term: Molarity of 69% HNO₃, density 1.41 g/mL? (Ex 1.6)
cards.definition: 1 L = 1410 g, HNO₃ = 972.9 g ÷ 63 = 15.44 M

cards.term: Molarity of 20 g sucrose in 2 L? (Ex 1.11)
cards.definition: 20/342 = 0.0585 mol ÷ 2 = 0.0293 M

cards.term: Mass of sodium acetate for 500 mL of 0.375 M? (Ex 1.5)
cards.definition: 0.1875 mol × 82.02 = 15.38 g

cards.term: 15 ppm CHCl₃ in water as mass %? (Ex 1.17)
cards.definition: 15/10⁶ × 100 = 1.5 × 10⁻³ %

cards.term: Molarity vs molality for dilute aqueous solutions? (intuition)
